title: Remote MCP clients use the kb directly and through a host MCP server
goal: Copilot Studio and other remote MCP clients can use the kb both ways, with one tool contract: directly, through _tools/kb_http.py serving the read-only tools over MCP Streamable HTTP (stateless, JSON responses, loopback behind an authenticating TLS proxy), and through a host MCP server that spawns kb_mcp.py over stdio and re-exposes kb_pack, kb_search and kb_show; both serve kb/public unless told otherwise, a test proves both paths give the same answers, and kb/_self documents each path and how to deploy it
notes: Two paths to Copilot Studio. First: the operator's TypeScript MCP server, already hosted over Streamable HTTP with authentication, spawns kb_mcp.py over stdio and re-exposes kb_pack, kb_search and kb_show (ST-2zvzr6gr); the TypeScript changes are planned in that server's own repository. Second: kb_http.py serves the kb directly behind a TLS proxy (ST-z6fw4er5, ST-y6ee5kdv). Operator answers: this repository delivers code, tests, docs and a runbook, not a deployment; the proxy authenticates and kb_http.py holds no secrets; a hosted or embedded kb serves kb/public unless told to serve more, one instance per audience, since root is a filter and not access control. Out of scope: a request or query log for hosted lookups (it touches the query log's redaction rules, an always-blocking gate), a container image or CI build, infrastructure as code, live-docs tools inside the server (TK-kgguzw2y). Later, once refined: an end-to-end proof that a Copilot Studio agent answers from the kb through each path, recorded as a report; research on the Dataverse MCP server and Dataverse Web API authentication (the kb has coverage none) if an agent is to use Dataverse beside the kb. TK-yittxcs5 (search_result blocks) must keep a text content block, which non-Claude clients such as Copilot Studio read. Scheduling: P2, in a sprint of its own planned once SP-z7a5c76b closes.
